```gherkin
# Generated by /feature-spec
# Feature: API Readiness Endpoint
# Stack: generic
# Assumptions: 4 (see api-readiness-endpoint_assumptions.yaml)
# Generated: 2026-08-11T09:30:00Z

@api-readiness-endpoint
Feature: API Readiness Endpoint
  As a platform operator
  I want to check whether the api_test service is ready to serve requests
  So that load balancers and orchestration systems route traffic only to a working service

  Background:
    Given the api_test service is running

  # Why: Core happy path — defines the readiness answer for a working service
  # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=medium] "Able to serve requests" means the service process is running and responsive; no external dependency checks are performed
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: Checking readiness of a service that is able to serve requests
    Given the service is able to serve requests
    When I request the readiness status
    Then the readiness check should succeed
    And the response should indicate the service is ready
    And the response should identify the service as "api_test"

  # Why: Health probes come from infrastructure, not signed-in users
  # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=low] The readiness endpoint requires no authentication
  @key-example
  Scenario: Readiness can be checked without signing in
    Given I am not signed in
    And the service is able to serve requests
    When I request the readiness status
    Then the readiness check should succeed

  # Why: The response contract is fixed — exactly the documented fields, nothing more
  # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=high] The readiness response contains only the ready indicator and the service name
  @boundary
  Scenario: The readiness response contains exactly the documented fields
    Given the service is able to serve requests
    When I request the readiness status
    Then the response should contain a ready indicator and a service name
    And the response should contain no other fields

  # Why: The readiness endpoint is read-only — attempts to submit data must be refused
  @negative @smoke
  Scenario: Attempting to submit data to the readiness endpoint is refused
    When I attempt to submit data to the readiness endpoint
    Then the request should be refused because the readiness endpoint is read-only
    And the readiness status should remain unchanged

  # Why: Readiness checks are pure reads and must not disturb the service
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Repeated readiness checks are consistent and side-effect free
    Given the service is able to serve requests
    When I request the readiness status several times in quick succession
    Then every readiness check should succeed
    And every response should indicate the service is ready

  # Why: Failure recovery — the endpoint must not falsely report readiness
  # [ASSUMPTION: confidence=low] A service that cannot serve requests does not report itself as ready
  @edge-case @negative
  Scenario: A service that is not able to serve requests does not report ready
    Given the service is not able to serve requests
    When I request the readiness status
    Then the response should not indicate the service is ready
```

```markdown
# Feature Spec Summary: API Readiness Endpoint

**Stack**: generic
**Generated**: 2026-08-11T09:30:00Z
**Scenarios**: 6 total (2 smoke, 0 regression)
**Assumptions**: 4 total (1 high / 1 medium / 2 low confidence)
**Review required**: Yes

## Scope

Specifies the readiness surface of the api_test service: a read-only readiness check that succeeds and reports the service as ready (identifying itself as "api_test") whenever the service is able to serve requests, and refusal of any attempt to submit data to the readiness endpoint. The response contract is fixed to exactly the ready indicator and the service name. Dependency-aware health checks, authentication, and additional response metadata are out of scope and carried as assumptions.
```
